listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Sunday, November 8. Here is what matters today. Our lead story. President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend Dana White. White runs the UFC. He says he plans to meet with the president on Monday. So far, those are the only confirmed facts. The offer has been made, and a meeting is set. Now the front page. Anthropic has filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission. It relates to a proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock. In Israel, the president has asked opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a government. Neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won enough support to command a majority. In Poland, six people were killed in a shooting in Krakow's main square. BBC reports that three more bodies were later found at the home of the attacker. Now the sections. In tech, the Claude Console now has a beta IP allowlist. It limits where a leaked API key can be used. Anthropic's public skills repository is also trending on GitHub. In politics, Democrats will run federal judicial appointments starting January third, after the change in the Senate majority. Meanwhile, the current Republican-led Congress still has to deal with the defense authorization act and a government funding bill. In world news, the Houthis say a Saudi air strike killed at least 33 people. Saudi Arabia has not commented. Separately, U.S. homelessness saw its largest drop in more than a decade, though it is still close to seven hundred thousand. In sports, the Houston Rockets lost to the Phoenix Suns, 102 to 99, after Devin Booker scored seven straight points late. DeForest Buckner returns to the Bay as the 49ers get ready for the Raiders. And Tatiana Suarez won a unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night, which puts her back in the title picture. In Atlanta, eight Black Democratic women expect to be sworn into statewide office in January after Tuesday's election. A Cobb County home development has also sold out, even with high interest rates. In architecture, Mach9 has added aerial LiDAR and photogrammetry support to its AI CAD software. LightYX has launched a connected workflow for layout and verification. In science, NASA announced new Moon Base awards, including a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE. And divers in Brazil are working to remove invasive sun coral that threatens native marine life. That is the brief. Have a good day. This is the Sunday edition. Here is the week in review. Democrats win Congress; Anthropic files for IPO. The midterms led the week. Democrats won full control of Congress for the first time since 2023 (w49). In Texas, Democrats flipped the U.S. Senate seat and the governor's office (w56). Democrat Annie Andrews won South Carolina's Senate race (w57). In Georgia, a record 2.8 million people voted early (w18). Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor (w51), Jon Ossoff won a second term (w65), and Democrats won control of the Georgia House (w73) and the Public Service Commission (w64). After the election, Stephen Miller was named to replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff (w119). Tech stocks lost about $2 trillion on fears of an AI crackdown (w94), then AI stocks climbed again (w121). Abroad, the U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island just before the vote (w24) while Qatar led talks with Iran (w2). A Russian strike on a Ukrainian aid site killed 29 people, and 48 were still missing (w59). After Israel's election ended without a clear winner, its president asked opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a government (w143). Paraguay's president was impeached after a bank collapse (w96), and a shooting in Krakow killed six people in the main square (w144). For your tools, Anthropic filed an S-1 for a proposed IPO (w50) and set up a Public Benefit Fund (w30). Message threads in the Messages API are now in beta (w25). Fast mode for Opus 4.8 will be removed on November 30 (w5). In AEC software, Qonic added AI agents to its BIM platform (w76) and Autom8Labs released agent skills for Revit (w67). lead.title: UFC's Dana White says he will meet with Trump Monday over offer to be White House press secretary
lead.note: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he has offered the job of White House press secretary to his friend Dana White, who runs the UFC. White said he plans to meet with the president on Monday. That meeting is the next step to watch, since the summary gives no sign yet that White has accepted or turned down the offer. The story matters to this reader on two fronts, politics and the UFC, because the head of the sport's biggest promotion could move into one of the most visible jobs in the White House. The press secretary is the administration's public voice, so a pick from outside the usual political ranks would stand out. For now there are only two confirmed facts: Trump made the offer, and the two men are due to meet Monday. Nothing more is established about the terms or timing of any decision.

week.headline: Democrats win Congress; Anthropic files for IPO
week.summary:
The midterms led the week. Democrats won full control of Congress for the first time since 2023 (w49). In Texas, Democrats flipped the U.S. Senate seat and the governor's office (w56). Democrat Annie Andrews won South Carolina's Senate race (w57). In Georgia, a record 2.8 million people voted early (w18). Keisha Lance Bottoms was elected governor (w51), Jon Ossoff won a second term (w65), and Democrats won control of the Georgia House (w73) and the Public Service Commission (w64). After the election, Stephen Miller was named to replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff (w119). Tech stocks lost about $2 trillion on fears of an AI crackdown (w94), then AI stocks climbed again (w121).

Abroad, the U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island just before the vote (w24) while Qatar led talks with Iran (w2). A Russian strike on a Ukrainian aid site killed 29 people, and 48 were still missing (w59). After Israel's election ended without a clear winner, its president asked opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form a government (w143). Paraguay's president was impeached after a bank collapse (w96), and a shooting in Krakow killed six people in the main square (w144).

For your tools, Anthropic filed an S-1 for a proposed IPO (w50) and set up a Public Benefit Fund (w30). Message threads in the Messages API are now in beta (w25). Fast mode for Opus 4.8 will be removed on November 30 (w5). In AEC software, Qonic added AI agents to its BIM platform (w76) and Autom8Labs released agent skills for Revit (w67). The Rockets moved into first place in the West, then lost two straight games (w26, w153).
